Which section each line item belongs to

Source: R/sections.R
assign_sections.Rd

Places every line item of a plan in the sections of an organization tree: brand and performance, lines of business, channels. sections holds the tree's leaves, each a target – the same named list of grain column = value(s) an op uses – or a list of targets. A line item is in a section when the section matches any of its rows.

Usage

assign_sections(plan, sections)

Arguments

plan

A MediaPlan.

sections

A named list, one entry per leaf section: its target, or a list of targets. Names must be distinct.

Value

A data frame with one row per line item (line_item_grain()):

line_item

Its key, as line_item() writes it.

section

The one section it is in; NA when it is in none, or in more than one.

n_matches

How many sections it is in.

Attributes overlaps (a data frame of line_item and sections, the sections' names joined with ", ") and unmatched (the line items in no section) list the disagreements, which also print beneath the table.

Details

A clean tree puts every line item in exactly one leaf. This reports where the plan and the tree disagree – line items in two leaves, line items in none – and never errors on either: whether an overlap is a mistake in the tree or a shared line, and whether an unplaced line item belongs to nobody or to a leaf not yet drawn, is the caller's decision.

A section may name a value the plan does not have (an organization names channels a plan has stopped buying), so values are matched leniently, as match_rows() with strict = FALSE. A column that is not in the grain is still an error: the organization's levels must be grain columns – add a missing level with regrain().

See also

match_rows(); check_budget() for a section's envelope.

Examples

plan <- media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(week = as.Date("2026-07-06"),
             channel = c("TV", "TV", "Search", "Social"),
             partner = c("NBC", "ESPN", "Google", "Meta"),
             planned_spend = c(50, 30, 40, 40)),
  grain = c("channel", "partner"), time = "week", name = "Q3"
)
assign_sections(plan, list(
  Video  = list(channel = "TV"),
  Search = list(channel = "Search"),
  Google = list(partner = "Google")   # overlaps Search
))
#>         line_item section n_matches
#> 1        TV | NBC   Video         1
#> 2       TV | ESPN   Video         1
#> 3 Search | Google    <NA>         2
#> 4   Social | Meta    <NA>         0
#> 1 in more than one section (Search | Google); 1 in none (Social | Meta).
